comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE: STAGE 3 — dispatched, the binding write never completed, and the failure is SWALLOWED

Investigated read-only against the tree, with a controlled in-process reproduction. The three
candidate stages this ticket named are now resolved to one.

### Stages 1 and 2 are RULED OUT, with citations

**Stage 1 (never planned) — ruled out.** `outbound_differ.compute_outbound_mutations`
(`outbound_differ.py:502-521`) has no knowledge of `filter_local_ids` at all: it iterates every
`local_tickets` entry and routes to `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` whenever
`binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id) is None` (`:509-521`). `run_differs.py:428-530` confirms the
differ receives the FULL unfiltered ticket set; filtering happens only afterward. **This also
falsifies the hypothesis I flagged as most likely** — that a filtered pass structurally cannot emit
a CREATE, which would have made this a harness defect. It is not.

**Stage 2 (planned but not dispatched) — ruled out.** The dispatch-narrowing filter
(`reconcile.py:396-411`, `reconcile_helpers.py:424-452`) builds `target_set = filter_local_ids ∪
{bound jira_key}` and matches on `Mutation.target`; an outbound CREATE carries
`target=om.local_id` (`run_differs.py:551-564`) — exactly the id in `filter_local_ids` — so it
always survives. `filter_local_ids` is never threaded into `applier.py`/`dispatch_one.py` (grepped:
no hits), so nothing re-filters downstream. The mode cap cannot drop it either: `_mode_sort_key`
(`apply_planning.py:45-64`) sorts outbound-creates FIRST precisely so a single create is never
capped out, and the cross-project guard and suppression both explicitly exclude creates
(`applier.py:258-281`, `apply_planning.py:120-131`).

### The mechanism

`create_one` (`dispatch_one.py:147-371`) is a write-ahead sequence: `bind_pending`+`save()` →
`create_issue` → `record_pending_key`+`save()` ← **this is where `get_jira_key` starts returning a
value** → `add_label`/`set_entity_property` → `bind_confirm`. Any exception before
`record_pending_key` succeeds leaves `get_jira_key` at `None`.

And the caller hides it. `_apply_one` (`applier.py:744-773`) re-raises only `HeadDriftError`,
`RescheduleError` and `urllib.error.HTTPError`; **every other exception type** falls to the generic
catch at `:770` and routes to `record_backstop_failure` (`apply_handlers.py:355-387`), which appends
a `bridge_state` alert, emits a `logger.warning` (not a `print`, so it may not even reach captured
stderr), returns an outcome carrying `"error"`, and **does not raise**. The pass continues and exits
normally.

### Reproduced, in-process, no live instance

Making `create_issue` raise a plain `ValueError` (a realistic DC rejection shape — issue-type /
screen / required-field mismatch) produced exactly the externally-observed signature:

    Traceback in stderr?: False
    RECON: batch_outcome action=create key=af8c-fake error='mutation-error: simulated: ...'
    binding after _apply_one: None

No traceback, no binding, pass completes — matching both harness runs.

### A useful narrowing from the ABSENCE of a traceback

`handle_create` (`apply_handlers.py:134-179`) soft-fails only a **404** `HTTPError`; any other
`HTTPError` is re-raised and WOULD print a top-level traceback (`__main__.py:697-701`). The runs
show no traceback, so the underlying failure was **not** a non-404 HTTPError — it was either a 404
(soft-failed by design) or a non-HTTP exception caught by the generic backstop.

### Verdict: PRODUCT defect, not a test-harness defect

The `--filter-local-ids` mechanism behaves identically to production and is not implicated. The gap
is that an outbound CREATE failure is treated as a routine silently-recorded mutation error with no
operator-visible signal beyond an alert file and a possibly-invisible log line — **which is exactly
this ticket's AC4**, and the same swallow class as [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] AC4 and the five
prior "silent success" bugs.

Note the compounding problem recorded on 39c1: the `bridge_alerts` entry this failure DOES write is
not read or uploaded by the DC harness or its workflow, so the one signal that exists is invisible
to the suite built to catch exactly this.

### Still open

The SPECIFIC underlying exception is not established — that needs the failing pass's
`bridge_state` alert-store contents or full stderr, neither of which the harness currently
surfaces. Falsifiers, stated: a run whose alert store shows ZERO `mutation-error` entries for the
local id AND `outbound_differ total=0 create=0` would point back to stage 1; a manifest showing the
create deferred past the cap would point to stage 2.

**Next step: make the harness surface the alert store** (the same change [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda]
needs), then re-run. That single change unblocks the specific diagnosis here AND 1a9f's AC1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## DIAGNOSTIC INSTRUMENTATION IS UP — Gerrit 1319

`assert_bridge_alert_for_mutation(cp, repo, local_id, *, key=None)` added to `_dc_support.py`, wired
into `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`.

The load-bearing property: it takes the pass's `CompletedProcess` as a REQUIRED argument and asserts
`returncode == 0` and no traceback BEFORE reading the alert store. Without that, an absent
`bridge_state/bridge_alerts/` directory is indistinguishable on disk from a clean pass that wrote
nothing (`alert_store.append` creates the directory only on first write) — so "no alert" could not
be told apart from "nobody looked".

**Diagnostic either way, which is why it is worth landing before the fix:**
 * an alert found → surfaces its `reason`, i.e. THE SPECIFIC SWALLOWED EXCEPTION this ticket's root
   cause could not name;
 * no alert on a provably-clean pass → a STRONGER finding: the create was never attempted, moving
   this bug from stage 3 back to stage 1/2 and contradicting the recorded root cause.

Design decision worth flagging: the helper RETURNS matching records rather than raising, so each
cell can build its own message — 18a5's two outcomes need different prose and baking that into a
shared helper would have made it less reusable.

Verified on current `gerrit/main` (not the agent's stale base): hygiene gate exits 0, ruff clean,
mypy 421 files, **58 live tests still collect** — the count is UNCHANGED, so no cell was added or
lost. Not in harness run 30857265932, which was already in flight; it lands for the next run.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE PROVEN — run 30867072561. The instrumentation did exactly what it was built for.

Change 1319's `assert_bridge_alert_for_mutation` took the pass's `CompletedProcess` as a REQUIRED argument and asserted `returncode == 0` BEFORE reading the alert store. That guard is what produced the answer:

    AssertionError: the pass exited 1, not 0 — a failed pass's alert store proves nothing
    about whether a MUTATION was swallowed, only that the pass itself did not complete.

    stderr: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 400
      url: http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/api/2/issue
      text: Field 'ticket_type' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown.,
            Field 'title' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown.,
            Field 'status' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown.

### THE DEFECT, NAMED

The outbound CREATE posts rebar's **LOCAL field names** — `ticket_type`, `title`, `status` — to `POST /rest/api/2/issue` as if they were Jira field ids. Jira's are `issuetype` and `summary`, and `status` is not settable at create at all (it is a workflow transition). DC rejects the whole request with 400, so no issue is created, so the binding is never written, so `get_jira_key` returns `None`.

**This is the STRONGER of the two outcomes comment 1 predicted.** No alert was the possibility that would move the bug 'from stage 3 back to stage 1/2' — and that is what happened, one stage further back than even that: the create is not merely unbound, the **entire pass aborts**. `get_jira_key returned None` was a symptom three steps downstream of the actual fault.

**It is NOT the pinned-template change (3fe5).** `ticket_type` and `title` are not Jira fields under ANY template or screen configuration — the error is 'or unknown', and they are unknown. Screen configuration cannot explain a field that does not exist. The same cell failed identically at baseline (run 30857265932), before the template was pinned; only the diagnosis improved.

### AC status

- [x] the failing STAGE is identified — **dispatch**, not bind: `reconcile_once` raises before any issue exists
- [x] the root cause is proven, not inferred — the 400 names all three offending fields verbatim
- [ ] the fix makes the cell GREEN on a live harness
- [ ] an outbound create that fails to bind surfaces an operator-visible signal rather than a pass

The last AC deserves emphasis given what was just learned: `reconcile_once` raising made the PASS exit 1, which is loud. But the cell that existed before 1319 read only `get_jira_key` and reported a missing binding — so a whole-pass abort was being read as a quiet binding failure. The instrumentation is the operator-visible signal this AC asks for, and it is already merged.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## THE FIX WORKED, AND THE CREATE NOW FAILS ONE LAYER DEEPER — run 30870845838

The three field names Data Center originally rejected are **GONE from the run entirely**: `Field 'ticket_type'/'title'/'status' cannot be set` does not appear anywhere in run 30870845838. The bridge-schema leak is fixed and live-confirmed.

The create still 400s, but on a **different and more specific error**:

    "errors":{"priority":"Could not find valid 'id' or 'name' in priority object.",
               "assignee":"data was not an object"}

That is genuine progress rather than a wash: the payload now gets past field-name validation and fails on field SHAPE. Two of three original errors are eliminated and the survivors are a different class.

### Root cause of the second layer

Both arrive as bare strings, and both for a reason:
 * the SHARED outbound mapper has already resolved rebar's integer priority to a Jira NAME (`LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` -> `"Medium"`), so a string reaches the transport;
 * Data Center identifies users by `name` rather than Cloud's accountId — which is why `validate_assignee_exists` returns the username on this transport.

Jira's REST API wants OBJECTS for both. ACLI accepts the bare forms, so the Cloud path never needed it. **That is the same per-transport seam a third time in one ticket** — the pass-through decision I approved for 'genuinely Jira-valid fields' was right about the NAMES and wrong about the SHAPES.

Fixed in Gerrit 1345: wrap only a non-empty **string**, so an already-object form is not nested a second time (a third distinct 400), and an absent field is never invented — injecting a default would assign the issue to nobody in particular, the create analogue of the mis-assignment bug 544e records on Cloud.

Gates: 2174 reconciler tests pass, ruff/mypy/hygiene clean.

- [x] the failing STAGE is identified — dispatch, not bind
- [x] the root cause is proven, not inferred — both layers, each named verbatim by Jira
- [ ] the cell is GREEN on a live harness — needs the next run, with 1345 in it
- [ ] an outbound create that fails to bind surfaces an operator-visible signal

# Outbound CREATE against DC produces no binding: `get_jira_key` returns None after the pass

## Provenance

Surfaced live by harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`) by story 5200's
NEW row-1-outbound cell (`test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`, landed in change
1283). Its author flagged the create-and-bind SETUP as the likeliest first failure precisely
because no prior live cell exercises an outbound CREATE against DC — every other outbound cell
mutates an issue that already exists and is already bound. The prediction was correct.

## Evidence — verbatim from the run

> the outbound pass did not create-and-bind '654e-8c11-d632-4a01' (get_jira_key returned None), so
> there is no DC issue to read the provenance markers off. Row 1's markers are written INSIDE the
> create (`dispatch_one.py:306-307`), so a missing binding is upstream of this oracle, not a marker
> finding.

The cell localises the failure itself: this is **not** a provenance-marker defect. The pass did not
produce a bound DC issue for the local ticket at all, so the oracle never got as far as reading
markers.

## Why this is filed rather than folded into 5200

5200's remaining work was "run the harness and read the verdicts"; this is a product finding the
run produced, and burying an unexplained outbound-create failure in a story's comment thread is how
a defect of this class survives. It is also the SIXTH instance of the epic's recurring shape —
"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half", every instance a SILENT success where the pass
reports OK.

## What is NOT yet established, stated plainly

Whether the create was never PLANNED (the differ emitted nothing for an unbound local ticket),
was planned but not DISPATCHED, or was dispatched and the binding write failed. Those are three
different defects. The harness output does not separate them, and `dispatch_one.py:571-578`-style
warn-and-continue swallowing means a dispatch failure would look identical to a planning gap from
the outside.

Note also that this cell is the ONLY live coverage of an outbound create against DC, so there is no
prior green run to bisect against — the path may never have worked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the failing STAGE is identified — planned / dispatched / bound — with the evidence that
      distinguishes it from the other two
- [ ] the root cause is proven, not inferred, and recorded here
- [ ] the fix makes `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers` GREEN on a live harness
      run, with the run id recorded
- [ ] an outbound create that fails to bind surfaces an operator-visible signal rather than a pass
      that reports OK (consistent with [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] AC4)
